title: Instruction Tuning (SFT)
summary: A base model continues text; an assistant answers. Supervised fine-tuning closes the gap by training on prompt-response examples with the same next-token loss, counted only on the response. This lesson covers chat templates, loss masking, data quality and quantity, packing and hyperparameters, and what SFT cannot fix.
objectives: Explain how a base model and an instruction-tuned model differ and why a small amount of SFT changes behaviour so much
Format a conversation with a chat template and explain why the template must match at inference
Compute the SFT loss with prompt tokens masked, and compare it with the unmasked loss
Estimate SFT training tokens, steps and compute, and compare them with pretraining
Choose packing, learning rate and epochs for SFT and recognise overfitting and forgetting
prerequisites: You should know the pretraining objective ([Pretraining Data](/learn/training-and-adaptation/pretraining-data)) and the memory cost of full fine-tuning ([Training at Scale](/learn/training-and-adaptation/training-at-scale)). Familiarity with tokens and special tokens ([Tokenization](/learn/model-foundations/tokenization)) helps with chat templates.
